title: Accessing non-static members inside a static method
answer: Yes, a static method can access non-static members when it has an explicit object reference; what it cannot do is access them directly through an implicit `this`, because no current instance exists in static context. The static method may create an object, receive one as a parameter, or use another reference and then call that object's instance methods or fields according to normal access rules.
